insight.title: Museum Stairs Are Intentionally Hard to Walk On
insight.subtitle: Wide, shallow steps are architecturally engineered to force your body into a posture of respect.
insight.notificationHook: Why museum stairs feel so awkward

sections.text: Have you ever struggled to walk gracefully up the wide, shallow stone steps of a museum or courthouse? You’re forced into an awkward, slow-motion stride that feels completely unnatural.
This isn’t a construction mistake. It’s "architectural choreography" designed to disrupt your natural rhythm, forcing your body to slow down, stand up straighter, and adopt a more dignified posture.
By altering your physical pace, the staircase acts as a mental decompression chamber, transitioning your brain from the chaotic rush of the street into a state of quiet contemplation.
They don’t just carry your body; they change your mindset.
